title: How To Count Past Infinity
subject: Mixed (math)
transcript_quality: auto-generated (aleph rendered as 'Alf', some misheard words), usable
beats: What's the biggest number you can think of? A googol, a googolplex?
Joke: the biggest number is a 40 planted in trees in Russia, by surface area
By amount, there's always 41, 42... no last number
Infinity isn't a number but a kind of number; some infinities are bigger
Cardinal numbers count things: 4 bananas, 20 dots
Same cardinality means you can pair members one to one
How many naturals? Not a natural; named aleph-null, the smallest infinity
Evens, odds and even fractions all have aleph-null members
Aleph-null beats any googolplex tower, yet we can count past it
Supertask: infinitely many shrinking lines in a finite space, matched to the naturals
Add one line: aleph-null plus one? No, re-pair and it's the same amount
Add two, three, even another infinity: still aleph-null
Same sequence made by sliding every other line to the end
Same amount, but clearly something differs. What?
Label lines in order and the extra line needs a label past every natural
Ordinals: omega is the next label; omega+1, omega+2
Finishing omega-th in a race: infinitely many finished before you
Order type: first ordinal not needed to label the set; same as cardinality for finite
In 'name the biggest number', omega+1 isn't bigger, just later
There are infinities with more things than aleph-null
List every subset of the naturals as yes/no rows
Diagonal argument: flip each diagonal entry to build an unlisted subset
Repeated power sets give ever bigger infinities
Wait: can we even treat an endless process as a finished whole?
Math vs science: axioms are true because we say so; invented or discovered?
Zermelo's axiom of infinity; reject it and you're a finitist
Reaching omega+omega needs another infinite set: a new ceiling
Axiom of replacement: swap every element for a banana and it's still a set
Replacement builds omega*2, omega squared, towers, epsilon-nought
All arrangements of aleph-null things have an order type: omega-1, so aleph-1
Where the power set falls is the continuum hypothesis; unknown
Climb: aleph-omega, aleph-omega-squared, an accelerating feedback loop
Nothing beyond? That's what we said about the finite
Aleph-null is a shadow of this: finite steps never reach it
Nothing to first infinity is like first infinity to an inaccessible
Large cardinal axioms, possible contradictions, open questions
Maybe no physical use; a tiny brain found something truer than the universe
